question.:question/problem:
Find the gradient of the product $f(x,y)g(x,y),$ given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =3 x - 4 y,\quad ∇f(x,y)=(3)\,i+(-4)\,j \\ g(x,y) & =x + 4 y,\quad ∇g(x,y)=(1)\,i+(4)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y)$ and $g(x,y)$ is given by

$$
∇[fg]=g∇f+f∇g.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y)g(x,y)] & =g(x,y)∇f(x,y)+f(x,y)∇g(x,y) \\  & =(x + 4 y)((3)\,i+(-4)\,j)+(3 x - 4 y)((1)\,i+(4)\,j) \\  & =(x + 4 y)(3)i+(x + 4 y)(-4)j+(3 x - 4 y)(1)i+(3 x - 4 y)(4)j \\  & =(3 x + 12 y)i+(- 4 x - 16 y)j+(3 x - 4 y)i+(12 x - 16 y)j \\  & =(6 x + 8 y)\,i+(8 x - 32 y)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((x+1){y}^{2})={y}^{2} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}((x+1){y}^{2})=2(x+1)y\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\text{ }j={y}^{2}\text{ }i+2(x+1)y\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{-({(x+1)}^{2}+{y}^{2})})=-2(x+1){e}^{-({(x+1)}^{2}+{y}^{2})} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{-({(x+1)}^{2}+{y}^{2})})=-2y{e}^{-({(x+1)}^{2}+{y}^{2})}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y) & =\frac{∂g}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂g}{∂y}\text{ }j=-2(x+1){e}^{-({(x+1)}^{2}+{y}^{2})}\text{ }i-2y{e}^{-({(x+1)}^{2}+{y}^{2})}\text{ }j.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2 x^{2} y z + x y z^{2})=4 x y z + y z^{2} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2 x^{2} y z + x y z^{2})=2 x^{2} z + x z^{2} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(2 x^{2} y z + x y z^{2})=2 x^{2} y + 2 x y z\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}j+\frac{∂f}{∂z}k=(4 x y z + y z^{2})\,i+(2 x^{2} z + x z^{2})\,j+(2 x^{2} y + 2 x y z)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{1}{x y z})=- \frac{1}{x^{2} y z} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{1}{x y z})=- \frac{1}{x y^{2} z} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{1}{x y z})=- \frac{1}{x y z^{2}}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂g}{∂x}i+\frac{∂g}{∂y}j+\frac{∂g}{∂z}k=(- \frac{1}{x^{2} y z})\,i+(- \frac{1}{x y^{2} z})\,j+(- \frac{1}{x y z^{2}})\,k\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem: Find the gradient of the product $f(x,y,z)g(x,y,z),$ given that $f(x,y,z)=4 x^{2} y^{2} z + 4 x y z^{3}$ and $g(x,y,z)=\frac{1}{x y z}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y,z)$ and $g(x,y,z)$ is given by

$$
∇[fg]=g∇f+f∇g.
$$

Now, we calculate the partial derivatives of $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4 x^{2} y^{2} z + 4 x y z^{3})=8 x y^{2} z + 4 y z^{3} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4 x^{2} y^{2} z + 4 x y z^{3})=8 x^{2} y z + 4 x z^{3} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(4 x^{2} y^{2} z + 4 x y z^{3})=4 x^{2} y^{2} + 12 x y z^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}j+\frac{∂f}{∂z}k=(8 x y^{2} z + 4 y z^{3})\,i+(8 x^{2} y z + 4 x z^{3})\,j+(4 x^{2} y^{2} + 12 x y z^{2})\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the partial derivatives of $g(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{1}{x y z})=- \frac{1}{x^{2} y z} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{1}{x y z})=- \frac{1}{x y^{2} z} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{1}{x y z})=- \frac{1}{x y z^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂g}{∂x}i+\frac{∂g}{∂y}j+\frac{∂g}{∂z}k=(- \frac{1}{x^{2} y z})\,i+(- \frac{1}{x y^{2} z})\,j+(- \frac{1}{x y z^{2}})\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Using the product rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y,z)g(x,y,z)] & =g(x,y,z)∇f(x,y,z)+f(x,y,z)∇g(x,y,z) \\  & =(\frac{1}{x y z})((8 x y^{2} z + 4 y z^{3})\,i+(8 x^{2} y z + 4 x z^{3})\,j+(4 x^{2} y^{2} + 12 x y z^{2})\,k)+(4 x^{2} y^{2} z + 4 x y z^{3})((- \frac{1}{x^{2} y z})\,i+(- \frac{1}{x y^{2} z})\,j+(- \frac{1}{x y z^{2}})\,k) \\  & =(\frac{1}{x y z})(8 x y^{2} z + 4 y z^{3})i+(\frac{1}{x y z})(8 x^{2} y z + 4 x z^{3})j+(\frac{1}{x y z})(4 x^{2} y^{2} + 12 x y z^{2})k+(4 x^{2} y^{2} z + 4 x y z^{3})(- \frac{1}{x^{2} y z})i+(4 x^{2} y^{2} z + 4 x y z^{3})(- \frac{1}{x y^{2} z})j+(4 x^{2} y^{2} z + 4 x y z^{3})(- \frac{1}{x y z^{2}})k \\  & =(8 y + \frac{4 z^{2}}{x})i+(8 x + \frac{4 z^{2}}{y})j+(\frac{4 x y}{z} + 12 z)k+(- 4 y - \frac{4 z^{2}}{x})i+(- 4 x - \frac{4 z^{2}}{y})j+(- \frac{4 x y}{z} - 4 z)k \\  & =(4 y)\,i+(4 x)\,j+(8 z)\,k\end{aligned}
$$
